points.heading: Deepen: choosing one or two words
points.body:
Today we put the whole week into one skill: **choosing**. You are the guide. First listen to what the sentence wants to say; then pick one word or two. We are not memorizing rare grammar names—we are learning to hear the sentence and decide. Your ear plus a time clue beats guessing from the first verb shape you remember. Ask three questions in order. Is there a closed moment like «yesterday at five»? → usually **one word** (canté). Does the result still matter now («already», «this week»)? → often **two words** (he cantado). Is it background or past habit? → imperfect **one word** (cantaba). Ask them one after another until the sentence feels right. Hear three mini-stories: «Terminé ayer» closes the past; «He terminado ya» keeps the result alive; «Leía cuando llamaron» paints background then a closed hit.

Look again at the example in the first sentence. Say what changes and what stays the same.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Práctica: Ahora te toca a ti.

Common mistake: Error común:

lesson.summary: This week we keep working on: Choose one word or two. Read each part calmly and try the activity.
lesson.memoryPhrase: One word: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two words: helper **haber** + already-done form (**he cantado**).
lesson.weekRecap: One word: canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría. Two words: helper haber + participle (he cantado). Learn to narrate WHEN an action happens: one-word forms and two-word forms, choosing with meaning.
lesson.priorDayRecap: Deepen: two-word times. We worked the two-word path: helper haber + participle (-ado/-ido), with he cantado, había cantado, and related forms.
